title: AIDA dispatch record
description: What is dispatched right now, at <task folder>/implementation/dispatch.json. One record per task since 2026-09-22 (live-run row 139). Before that it was one per project, at <project path>/dispatch.json, which made a second task's build wait on the first. The build of one task is serial, so a task has at most one active dispatch. `dispatch-open` refuses to overwrite one already there, and `dispatch-close` removes it. Two tasks of one project each hold their own. This is the one record two PreToolUse hooks read to tell a dispatched role's own guardrails apart from a person working their own repository: hooks/deny-prior-source.sh (a test author reading past its own interface record) and hooks/deny-frozen-test-writes.sh (anyone writing to a test this task already froze, and since 2026-09-19 an implementer writing under codePath outside the files its unit owns, read from `ownedFiles`). Neither hook writes this file; the implement skill writes it immediately before a dispatch and clears it immediately after, through implement-actions.sh's own `dispatch-open` and `dispatch-close` actions. Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

role.description: The dispatched agent's own plugin-scoped type, matched by both hooks against a payload's `agent_type` field. hooks/deny-prior-source.sh applies this record's denied reads to this role and to no other, and since 2026-09-11 an agent whose type is not this role is allowed through a `systemMessage` naming both values, rather than in silence: that is the case a mistyped or unnamed dispatch lands in. hooks/deny-frozen-test-writes.sh does not gate on this field, because a frozen test is protected from every role. It reads this field only to report the one exception it makes: a test author writing its own unit's frozen test is allowed, and when the reported agent type is not the role recorded here the allow says so through a `systemMessage`. A plugin's agent reports that type as `<plugin>:<agent>` as well as the bare name, so a hook matches both forms; this field itself stores whichever form the dispatch was opened with, since a hook does the pattern matching, not this record. There is no value here for a person working the main thread: the main thread carries no `agent_type` at all, so it can never match a role recorded here, whatever this field says. That absence is what keeps a person editing their own repository from being read as a dispatched builder.

task.description: The task id this dispatch belongs to, the same value task.json's own `id` carries. The record lives in that task's own implementation folder, beside the frozen test records deny-frozen-test-writes.sh reads. A hook finds the record as the one whose codePath holds the payload's working directory (scripts/lib/paths.sh, dispatch_record_for). It reads this field to report which task holds it.

openedAt.description: When `dispatch-open` wrote this record, UTC, to the second. Set by the script, never typed. A record left by a role that never returned looks like a live one otherwise. `dispatch-open` reads this and names the age in its refusal once the record is over a day old (live-run row 139). Nothing clears a stale record on its own: a person runs `dispatch-close`.

resumedAt.description: Present once the role returned with no report and `dispatch-close --no-report` kept the record open for one resume by message, UTC, to the second (gap row 228). `dispatch-open --resume` writes it at once, equal to openedAt, when the earlier record was already closed. A second `--no-report` on a record carrying it halts the order and removes the record (exit 110).

reportPath.description: Present when the role's brief pins a file (gap rows 228 and 250): the reviewer's findingsPath or verdictsPath, or the fixer's or test author's reportPath. `dispatch-open` copies it from the brief. A plain `dispatch-close` refuses the reviewer's record while the file is missing or no newer than the record (exit 111), and runs the fixer's or test author's as `--no-report` does (exit 112).

completionLine.description: Present beside reportPath on a fixer's or test author's record (gap row 250): the line the role writes last in its report. A plain `dispatch-close` needs the report to end with it and to hold one other line, and a fixer's report to be no older than the last commit in codePath.

unit.description: The work order id this dispatch is for. deny-frozen-test-writes.sh compares this against the unit that owns a frozen test file being written: a test author dispatched for this unit may write this unit's own tests, and never an earlier unit's.

codePath.description: The code repository this dispatch runs in, copied from the project's own project.json at the moment the dispatch opened. Both hooks resolve every relative path below against this value, since a dispatched agent's working directory is not guaranteed to be codePath itself. hooks/deny-frozen-test-writes.sh resolved a relative write target against that working directory alone until 2026-09-11, which contradicted this field: the frozen paths it compares against are resolved from codePath, so a relative write from any other directory normalized to a path it could not match. It now resolves a relative write target against codePath first, and against the working directory the payload reports second when that directory is not codePath. A match on either resolution refuses the write. The second test stays because a shell command's own relative path is really relative to the directory the command runs in, and a frozen test must be refused on either reading.

denyRead.description: Paths under codePath a test author may not read, relative to codePath. hooks/deny-prior-source.sh denies a Read whose target falls under one of these, or under one of these itself, for the dispatched role only. Empty means nothing is denied, which is not the same as no dispatch being open: an open dispatch with an empty list still answers hook queries, the hook allows every read, and it reports that it could enforce nothing rather than passing in silence. For the test-author role the list is never assembled by a caller: `dispatch-open` derives it from the owned files every work order in the frozen snapshot declares and the paths they reuse, less this order's own test files, and refuses when no production source is in it.

allowWrite.description: Paths under codePath the dispatched role is meant to write, relative to codePath. Recorded for a person or a later check reading this file to see what the dispatch was for; neither hook enforces it today. deny-frozen-test-writes.sh decides a write by whether the target is a path this task already froze, or by `ownedFiles` below, not by whether it appears here.

denyCommand.description: Present on a test author's record since gap row 231: the shell command forms that read the shape of code through a runtime, such as `php:eval` or `ReflectionClass`. `dispatch-open` copies them from scripts/introspection-forms.txt and never takes them by hand. hooks/deny-prior-source.sh refuses a Bash command that holds one as a whole word, heredoc bodies included, for the dispatched role only. A script the role writes to a file and then runs passes, because its text never reaches the command.

ownedFiles.description: Present on an implementer's record since 2026-09-19 (live-run row 92), and on a fixer's since 2026-09-21 (live-run row 116): the files its work order owns in the frozen snapshot, relative to codePath, derived by `dispatch-open` and never passed by hand. A fixer's list also holds the `allowedFiles` of the round's fix brief, the paths a person granted with `fix-brief --allow`. hooks/deny-frozen-test-writes.sh reads it as its second rule while this record names the implementer or the fixer. A write to a path under codePath that is not one of these files, or under one of these directories, is refused. The reason tells the role to stop and report. A path outside codePath, the task folder where the report and the interface record live, is not judged. The same list sits in allowWrite for this role; it is repeated here because allowWrite also takes hand-passed paths and is enforced by nothing, and a write bound must come from the snapshot alone.
